# i3dnet_cdn_resource (Resource)

Manages an i3D.net CDN resource: a set of public hostnames that the CDN serves from one or more origins.

The resource manages the hostnames, the origins, the flags and an optional predefined allowlist. Every setting is read back from the CDN API, so a plan shows changes made outside Terraform, for example in the CDN dashboard, and an apply puts them back.

Point each hostname at the CDN with a CNAME record to `cname_target`.

The provider needs a CDN API key (`cdn_api_key`) for this resource. The key belongs to one group and initiative, and the resource must use the same `group_code` and `initiative_code`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
provider "i3dnet" {
  cdn_api_key = var.cdn_api_key
}

# The hostname www.example.com, served by the CDN from one origin.
resource "i3dnet_cdn_resource" "www" {
  name            = "www"
  group_code      = "my-group"
  initiative_code = "my-initiative"

  hostnames = [{
    fqdn   = "www.example.com"
    ssl_cn = "wildcard.example.com"
  }]

  origins = [{
    fqdn        = "origin.example.com"
    healthcheck = { path = "/healthz" }
  }]

  flags = {
    auth_pass_through = true
  }
}

# Point the hostname at the CDN with a CNAME record, in whichever DNS
# provider manages the zone.
output "cname_target" {
  value = i3dnet_cdn_resource.www.cname_target
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `group_code` (String) Code of the CDN group the resource belongs to. Must be the group of the provider's CDN API key. Cannot be changed after creation.
- `hostnames` (Attributes List) Public hostnames the CDN serves. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--hostnames))
- `initiative_code` (String) Code of the CDN initiative the resource belongs to. Must be the initiative of the provider's CDN API key. Cannot be changed after creation.
- `name` (String) Name of the CDN resource, as shown in the CDN dashboard. 1 to 50 characters.
- `origins` (Attributes List) Origins the edges fetch content from. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--origins))

### Optional

- `flags` (Attributes) Switches for the resource. Every flag has a default, so the block is optional. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--flags))
- `predefined_allowlist` (String) Key of a predefined allowlist that limits who can reach the resource. The `i3dnet_cdn_predefined_allowlists` data source lists the keys. When not set, the resource is open to everyone. When set, Terraform sends the allowlist to the CDN API before the hostnames and flags, and removes it only after them.
- `strategy` (String) How the edges pick an origin: `HASH`, `FALLBACK` or `RANDOM`. Defaults to `HASH`.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `cname_target` (String) Target for each hostname's CNAME record.
- `id` (String) UID of the CDN resource.

<a id="nestedatt--hostnames"></a>
### Nested Schema for `hostnames`

Required:

- `fqdn` (String) The hostname, without a trailing dot.
- `ssl_cn` (String) Name of the edge TLS certificate that covers `fqdn`. The API does not check that the certificate exists, so a wrong name shows up only as failing HTTPS.


<a id="nestedatt--origins"></a>
### Nested Schema for `origins`

Required:

- `fqdn` (String) Host name or IP address of the origin.
- `healthcheck` (Attributes) How the edges check that the origin is healthy. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--origins--healthcheck))

Optional:

- `dns_record` (String) How the origin's address is resolved: `A` or `SRV`. Defaults to `A`.
- `location` (String) Region of the origin: `EU`, `NAW`, `NAE` or `APAC`. Defaults to `EU`.
- `port` (Number) Port of the origin. Defaults to `443`.
- `ssl` (Boolean) Whether the edges connect to the origin over TLS. Defaults to `true`.
- `verify_ssl` (Boolean) Whether the edges verify the origin's TLS certificate. Defaults to `true`.

<a id="nestedatt--origins--healthcheck"></a>
### Nested Schema for `origins.healthcheck`

Required:

- `path` (String) Path the health check requests, for example `/healthz`.

Optional:

- `expected_status_code` (Number) HTTP status a healthy origin returns. Defaults to `200`.
- `host` (String) Base URL the health check requests `path` from. When not set, it is the origin's own URL: `https://<fqdn>`, or `http://<fqdn>` when `ssl` is false.
- `interval_ms` (Number) Milliseconds between checks. At least `15000`, the default.
- `min_valid_checks` (Number) Number of passing checks after which the origin counts as healthy. Defaults to `2`.
- `timeout_ms` (Number) Milliseconds a check may take. Defaults to `2000`.



<a id="nestedatt--flags"></a>
### Nested Schema for `flags`

Optional:

- `auth_pass_through` (Boolean) Whether the edges forward the `Authorization` request header to the origin. Defaults to `false`.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the CDN serves the resource. Defaults to `true`.
- `force_https` (Boolean) Whether the edges redirect HTTP requests to HTTPS. Defaults to `true`.
- `override_backend_host` (Boolean) Whether the edges send the origin's own `fqdn` as the `Host` header instead of the public hostname. Defaults to `true`.
- `override_health_host` (Boolean) Whether health checks send the origin's own `fqdn` as the `Host` header. Defaults to `true`.
- `use_i3d_static_dns` (Boolean) Whether the resource uses i3D.net's static DNS. Defaults to `false`.


<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a CDN resource by its UID.
terraform import i3dnet_cdn_resource.www <uid>
```
